questions.q: What is the status of TDE on Overlook's database immediately after Chapter 2's Bicep deployment?
options: It must be manually enabled before any data can be stored
It is already on by default — every new Azure SQL Database is TDE-encrypted at rest from the moment it's created
It requires a separate paid add-on
It only applies to Managed Instance, not Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: TDE is on by default for every new Azure SQL Database, so OverlookDB has been encrypted at rest since Lesson 6's deployment finished.

options: Data in memory while a query is running
Data in transit between the application and the database
Data at rest — the physical data files, log files, and backups on storage
Only column names and table schemas
questions.explain: TDE operates at the storage layer, below the query engine, protecting files and backups at rest — not data in memory or in transit.

questions.q: Would TDE alone stop an authorized scheduling-app account from reading a patient's chart with a normal SELECT statement?
options: Yes, TDE blocks all SELECT statements against encrypted data
No — TDE protects against someone stealing the physical storage or a backup file directly; it does nothing to stop an authorized, logged-in account's normal query
Yes, but only for Managed Instance
No, because TDE is not actually enabled by default
questions.explain: TDE is about protecting stolen storage/backups, not about restricting what an authorized account can query — that's a different layer of control entirely.

questions.q: What is the difference between service-managed keys and BYOK (Bring Your Own Key)?
options: There is no real difference
Service-managed keys are handled internally by Azure with no setup; BYOK stores the TDE protector in the customer's own Azure Key Vault, giving the customer ultimate control including revocation
BYOK is required for every Azure SQL database
Service-managed keys only work for test environments
questions.explain: Overlook's capstone stays with the service-managed default; BYOK is a real alternative for stricter compliance requirements, not part of this mandate.

questions.q: What T-SQL query confirms TDE is actually active on OverlookDB, and what result confirms it?
options: SELECT * FROM sys.databases; checking for a column named TDE
A query against sys.dm_database_encryption_keys joined to sys.databases, checking for encryption_state = 3
There is no way to confirm TDE status with T-SQL
EXEC sp_helpdb, checking for a status of ENCRYPTED
questions.explain: sys.dm_database_encryption_keys reports encryption_state, where 3 means Encrypted — the real, verifiable confirmation this lesson uses.
